103-pit-universe-from-repo-git-history.provides: A POINT-IN-TIME VENUE UNIVERSE, reconstructed for free from the git history of a hardcoded ticker list in a public repo. THE DESK GAP THIS ANSWERS IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD: 'exchangeInfo is a look-ahead in the UNIVERSE' (free-data-miner 2026-08-12) -- the live endpoint returns TODAY's symbol set and nothing else, so any backtest that builds its universe from it silently excludes every name that has since been removed. A stale hardcoded list is the inverse artifact: it is a DATED ATTESTATION that a set of symbols was tradeable when it was written, and git history turns one such file into a TIME SERIES of universes. MEASURED HERE (vintage -> names absent from live exchangeInfo, 865 symbols / 731 TRADING): 2020-06-28 n=25 -> 1 gone; 2023-03-07 n=213 -> 55 gone; 2023-12-05 n=202 -> 50; 2025-11-14 n=199 -> 48.
103-pit-universe-from-repo-git-history.the_number_that_matters: 8.7% TRUE USDT-perp survivorship erasure, NOT the headline 25.8%. Of the 55 names in the 2023-03-07 vintage now absent, 40 are BUSD-quote pairs killed by the BUSD wind-down -- a QUOTE-CURRENCY retirement, not a delisting -- leaving 15 of 173 USDT names = 8.7%. AND 3 OF THOSE 15 ARE REBRANDS WITH A CONTINUING PRICE SERIES, confirmed against live exchangeInfo: MATICUSDT->POLUSDT (TRADING), RNDRUSDT->RENDERUSDT (TRADING), TOMOUSDT->VICUSDT (SETTLING). So ~6.9% genuine removal + ~1.7% rename. A RENAME AND A DELISTING ARE OPPOSITE EVENTS THAT LOOK IDENTICAL IN A SYMBOL-SET DIFF: treat a rename as a death and you book a phantom delisting; ignore it and you sever a live series.
103-pit-universe-from-repo-git-history.how_to_use: (1) As a SURVIVORSHIP CONTROL: any universe built from live exchangeInfo is missing ~7% of the 2023 USDT cross-section by construction, and the missing names are non-random (they died). (2) As a RENAME MAP: the diff between adjacent vintages proposes rename candidates that are then confirmed one call at a time against exchangeInfo status. (3) GENERALISES FLEET-WIDE AND COSTS NOTHING: every region has repos with hardcoded symbol/ticker lists, and every one of them is a dated universe snapshot its author never intended to publish. The older and DEADER the repo, the better the vintage -- this is the one axis where an abandoned repo beats a maintained one.
103-pit-universe-from-repo-git-history.limits_stated_honestly: This is an AUTHOR's universe, not the exchange's: it is a LOWER BOUND on what was listed (names in it existed) and says nothing about names the author omitted. Every current caller compares a live clock to a live clock and is correct; any future caller that converts HISTORY with that scalar is wrong by exactly 1 hour for roughly five months of every year, and the errors sit precisely on the DST seams.

The tape's index dtype is datetime64[ms, UTC] -- the label asserts a timezone the data does not have (already documented at desks/mt5/research/h1_source.py:195). Any join to a genuinely-UTC source (FRED, LBMA, macro calendars) is misaligned by 2-3h unless converted.
Assuming EET/EEST is wrong in the ~3 March weeks and ~1 autumn week when the US and EU calendars disagree.

norgesbank_gov_fx_transactions.mechanism: STATUTORY FORCED FLOW. Under Norway's fiscal rule Norges Bank must convert a pre-announced, fixed NOK amount every business day on behalf of the Ministry of Finance, smoothed over the month, regardless of price. WHO IS FORCED: the central bank itself, by mandate — it cannot stop, cannot time, and pre-commits publicly. The daily amount is known in advance, so the tradable object is the ANNOUNCEMENT SURPRISE (change in the daily amount vs the prior month) at a fixed clock.

norgesbank_gov_fx_transactions.verification: THREE-FOR-THREE EXACT MATCH between the statistics table and the independently-worded monthly press releases: Aug-2026 table -350 vs PR 'sell FX equivalent to NOK 350 million per day'; Jul-2026 -400 vs 400; May-2026 -100 vs 100. failure_modes: THE STATISTICS TABLE OMITS THE SECOND LEG. It carries ONLY the government/petroleum leg. True total Aug-2026 net daily FX sale is 474 m, not 350 m: a user of the table alone understates the actual flow by 35%. Only the PRESS RELEASE carries both legs. SLUG DATE != EVENT DATE. Press release 2026?/2021-08-30-fx has article:published_time = 2021-08-31. A scraper joining on the URL slug is off by one day for at least this event. Read published_time, never the slug.
article:published_time is LOCAL Oslo wall-clock with no zone marker and a U+202F narrow no-break space before AM/PM — naive strptime fails on the separator and naive UTC assumption is off by 1-2h.

THREE DATES CARRY '..' RATHER THAN A VALUE: 2024-06-30, 2024-12-30, 2025-06-30. Under the producer's own footnote a date only APPEARS if an intervention occurred -- so these are a THIRD state, 'intervention occurred, value not (yet) published', distinct from both 'no intervention' (absent) and a number. Dropping '..' collapses it into 'no intervention' and silently fabricates three quiet half-year-ends. This is the desk's recurring class: a producer computes a distinction and the consumer collapses it.

LIVENESS IS max(valued observation) = 2022-12-30, NOT the 'updated' stamp of 2026-07-02 and NOT tableinfo's latestPeriod of 2025-06-30. Three different fields give three different answers and only one is the data. (Run (g)'s lesson, second instance.)

The defensible use is as a CLEAN, FORCED, DAILY MEASURE OF SAFE-HAVEN FLOW INTO A EUR-PERIPHERY PEG, tested on EURSEK/EURNOK/EURCHF/EURUSD -- a cross-instrument conditioning variable, not a DKK trade.

verification.method: THE EMU IRREVOCABLE-CONVERSION ORACLE. After 1999-01-01 each legacy currency was locked to the euro at a published rate, so legacy_quote x conversion_rate MUST equal the EUR quote to rounding. Ten of eleven reproduce it at a median 0.01-0.54 bp over 795 days (DEM 0.01, NLG 0.01, FRF 0.02, FIM 0.02, IEP 0.03, ATS 0.05, ESP 0.06, PTE 0.07, BEF 0.13, ITL 0.54).
verification.control_that_should_fail_and_did: GRD is off by a median 312 bp for 1999-2000 and snaps to 0.15 bp from 2001-01-01 -- Greece joined the euro two years after the others. The one series that should disagree does, on the right date.
verification.anti_synthesis_control: Pre-1999 deviations are 146-355 bp median (max 2,542 bp) -- so these are genuine independent quotes, NOT legacy prices back-synthesised from the euro. A vendor that had synthesised them would show ~0 bp before 1999 too, which is impossible.

known_failure_modes: SEKEURPMI carries 1,506 observations BEFORE the euro existed (1993-01-04 -> 1998-12-31). Those are ECU basket quotes published under a series labelled EUR: a silent definitional splice covering 18% of the series, with no flag anywhere in the API.
GRD before 2001-01-01 is a floating quote inside a series that looks locked for the rest of its life.
riksbank_swea_pre_euro_legacy_fx.method_generalisation: The EMU conversion rates are a FREE GROUND-TRUTH ORACLE for any legacy-currency series from any source, and they test both directions: post-1999 agreement proves scale/units, pre-1999 DISagreement proves the quotes are not synthetic.
